chunks: My father narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah ibn Abi Khalaf Al-Qummi Al-Ash'ari, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Musa ibn Qasim Al-Bajali, from someone who narrated to him, from Murazim, who said:

I asked Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) about praying in the Mosque of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: One prayer in my mosque is equal to one thousand prayers elsewhere, and one prayer in Masjid al-Haram is equal to one thousand prayers in my mosque.
Then he said: Verily Allah has given preference to Makkah, and He has made some parts of it better than others, saying: 'And take for yourselves a place of prayer on the standing-place of Ibrahim'.
And He said: Verily Allah has given preference to some people, and He ordered following them and loving them in the Book.

key_terms.مَسْجِدِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: Mosque of the Messenger of Allah
key_terms.مَوَدَّتِهِمْ: Loving them (referring to the preferred people/Imams)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward multiplier for praying in the Prophet's Mosque versus Masjid al-Haram?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the hierarchical sanctity of Islamic spaces, elevating the Prophet's Mosque above general mosques and Masjid al-Haram above the former, a distinction rooted in divine preference. It connects these physical sanctuaries to the spiritual authority of the Ahl al-Bayt by citing the Quranic command to take the Maqam Ibrahim as a place of prayer, thereby linking the physical act of worship with the theological imperative of following the chosen people.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 2. My father narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Abī Khalaf Al-Qummi Al-Ash’ari, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Mūsā ibn Qāsim Al-Bajali, from someone who narrated to him, from Murāzim, who said:

I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) about praying in the Mosque of the Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.). Imam (a.s.) replied: The Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.) has said: One Salāt in my mosque is equal to one thousand prayers elsewhere, and one Salāt in MASJID AL-ḤARĀM is equal to one thousand prayers in my mosque.

Then Imam (a.s.) continued: Verily Allāh has given preference to Makkah over other cities, and He has given preference to (specific) areas (of Makkah) over other areas in it by saying, “Take for yourselves a place of prayer on the standing-place of Ibrāhīm” [2:125].
Allāh has also given preference to some people over others, and in His Book He has ordered people to follow them and to love them.
